title: Self-supervised pseudo-lesion pretraining improves pancreatic cancer detection on CT
summary: A self-supervised pseudo-lesion segmentation step was used to train CNN and transformer models on CT from 4,287 patients with pancreatic cancer. Internal accuracy was 94.3% (CNN) and 95.7% (transformer); on 361 external cross-racial patients it was 82.5% and 87.8%. With only 10% of the training data, pretraining raised accuracy by 20.5% and sensitivity by 37.0%. The study is retrospective and external accuracy is lower.
ai_technology: Self-supervised pseudo-lesion segmentation pretraining for CNN and transformer classifiers

evidence.tested: Internal validation and cross-racial external validation on open-access CT (n=361).
evidence.unknown: Prospective and reader-study performance are not reported; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Trained models with limited annotation to classify pancreatic cancer.
